summary: The Read Restrictions sync on 4 August 2026 again asked for review of the spec, API and end-to-end PRs, then discussed nested or conflicting masks. Prashant presented a survey of comparable systems. Daniel asked for concrete examples and for a safe order of operations; Nevin, Laurent, Corey and Sung supported disabling the behavior in the spec for now, with care about how rules are relaxed later. Prashant is to start a thread, time-boxed to one or two weeks, weighing 'disallow nested' against a defined safe evaluation order.

topics.title: Request for review: spec, API and E2E
topics.summary: The agenda asked for review of the read restrictions spec PR, the API PR and the end-to-end PR. The action items repeat the request to everyone.

topics.title: Nesting and conflicting masks
topics.summary: Prashant had surveyed how comparable systems handle nesting or conflicting masks. Daniel asked for clarifying examples; the major one is inner versus outer null masking rules, and he thought out loud about an inner-to-outer order. Nevin supported disabling the behavior in the spec for now: read restrictions are a contract between the catalog or policy engine and the client, catalogs, policy engines and end users should carry more responsibility for sensible outcomes, and the restriction can be relaxed later; he wanted a concrete proposal with scope and effort before considering an evaluation order. Laurent supported disabling it in the spec and delegating conflicts to the catalog or authorizer, Corey supported the direction but warned to be careful about how rules are relaxed later, and Sung favored being restrictive for now with future discussion. Prashant asked Daniel for a concrete ask: a deep dive on what policy engines do, or an order of operations that is safe and consistent.
open_questions: Disallow nested restrictions (safe and simple, possibly a client exception on an invalid restriction set), or define an execution order that is generally safe?
Is there a definable, bottom-up execution order, like an expression tree, that always works across policy engines?
Which responsibilities belong to the catalog and policy engine versus the client or execution engine?

action_items.what: All: review the spec and implementations (apache/iceberg#13879, #16198, #16131).
Start a thread on nested restrictions, time-boxed to 1-2 weeks until the next sync, covering option A (disallow nested) and option B (Daniel's ask for a preferred safe order of operations).
